hints.content:
The opposite angles in ANY inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary.  [[☃ explanation 1]]

>$\text{m}\angle FPI = 180^\circ-110^\circ = 70^\circ$

options.explanation:
The measure of an inscribed angle is $\frac{1}{2}$ of the measure of the arc that it intercepts.

$\pink{\text{m}\angle P} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FL} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{LI})$  
$\blue{\text{m}\angle L} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{IP} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{PF})$

When we add the measures of the two angles together, something interesting happens:

$\pink{\text{m}\angle P}+ \blue{\text{m}\angle L} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FL} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{LI}) + \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{IP} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{PF})$

$\pink{\text{m}\angle P} + \blue{\text{m}\angle L} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FL} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{LI} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{IP} + \text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{PF})$

The sum of those $4$ arcs makes up the entire circle, which is $360^\circ$.

$\pink{\text{m}\angle P} + \blue{\text{m}\angle L} = \frac{1}{2}(360) = 180$

hints.content:
The angle $\angle FPI$ is an inscribed angle that intercepts  $\stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FI}$.

The measure of an inscribed angle is half the measure of the arc that it intercepts.

>$\text{m} \stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FI}=2(\green{70^\circ})=140^\circ$

The arc measure of $\stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FI}$ is equal to the sum of the measures of $\stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FL}$ and $\stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{LI}$.  So:

>$\text{m}\stackrel{\LARGE{\frown}}{FL}=140^\circ-97^\circ$
